root_cause: CONSOLE_HTML_FORMAT puts the monospace font stack on <pre style="font-family:Menlo,..."> but the inner <code> element has no font-family, so the browser user-agent stylesheet (code { font-family: monospace }) overrides the inherited stack. Box-drawing glyphs then render in a different font and right-hand borders misalign in exported HTML (issue #3104, Chrome on macOS).
best_solution:
In rich/_export_format.py change the single template line `
{code}
` to `
{code}
`. An inline style attribute on beats the user-agent rule and makes inherit the 
 font stack. Nothing else changes: the
acceptable_alternatives: None under the hidden tests. They compare the full HTML string, so a CSS rule `code { font-family: inherit; }` in the <style> block works in a browser but fails the tests. Only the inline attribute written exactly as `style="font-family:inherit"` (no space, no semicolon) passes.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_console.py::test_export_html, test_export_html_inline and test_save_html compare the whole exported HTML to an exact string that contains `<code style="font-family:inherit">` right after `<pre style="font-family:Menlo,'DejaVu Sans Mono',consolas,'Courier New',monospace">`. Every other byte (no leading newline, same <style> block) must stay the same. The SVG export tests (test_export_svg, test_save_svg) must keep passing.
locating_signals: Nothing in the statement: it is only 'Fix #3104' and 'See #3104' plus the PR checklist. The linked issue title ('font-family ignored in html_export due to user agent stylesheet for <code>') and its body name the fix. With that text, grepping for '<code>' or 'font-family:Menlo' finds CONSOLE_HTML_FORMAT in rich/_export_format.py. No function is named; the fix is a module-level template constant.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4 (100 calls, 103s) and v7 (60 calls, 189s) returned empty patches. v6 (68 calls) changed one entry in rich/_cell_widths.py (73104-73105 width 0 to 1), which has nothing to do with the bug, so the 3 HTML tests still failed. v8 (70 calls) found the right file and the right idea (font-family: inherit on code) but wrote it as a `code {{ font-family: inherit; }}` CSS rule in the <style> block, not as the inline attribute. It also removed the `\` after the opening triple quote (output now starts with a newline), rewrote CONSOLE_SVG_FORMAT into a foreignObject template with a new {stylesheet} key, deleted the _SVG_FONT_FAMILY/_SVG_CLASSES_PREFIX constants and left a reproduce_issue.py file behind. Result: 6 failures, including test_export_svg/test_save_svg with KeyError: 'stylesheet' and test_save_html failing on the leading newline.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only 'Fix #N' with no body, the spec is effectively hidden, so keep risk low: (1) search the repo for the symptom's vocabulary (CHANGELOG, tests, docs, templates) before editing; (2) never make speculative edits to unrelated data tables or files just to produce a non-empty diff; (3) keep the change to the smallest edit on the one element or line involved, and match the style of nearby code, e.g. an inline style attribute when the sibling element already uses one, not a new stylesheet rule. Output templates are usually checked by exact-string tests, so do not touch whitespace, line continuations or neighbouring templates, and never rewrite or delete constants you were not asked to change. Before submitting, run the existing tests for that module to confirm nothing else broke, and delete scratch repro scripts.
